intro: Madagascar, the world's fourth-largest island, was settled by seafarers from Borneo and Africa and has wildlife found nowhere else.

chapters.title: Settlers from afar
text: People arrived surprisingly late, within the last 2,000 years or so. Austronesian sailors from Southeast Asia, probably from Borneo, and Bantu-speaking Africans both settled; the Malagasy language is related to languages of Borneo.

chapters.title: The Merina kingdom
text: In the 1800s the Merina kingdom, ruled from Antananarivo, united most of the island. Queen Ranavalona I resisted European influence.

highlight.title: Queens
highlight.text: Four queens ruled Madagascar in the 1800s.

chapters.title: French rule and independence
text: France conquered Madagascar in 1895. A 1947 uprising was brutally crushed. Madagascar became independent in 1960. Political crises have been frequent; in October 2025 youth protests and a military unit forced President Andry Rajoelina out.

keyTerms.meaning: The people and language of Madagascar.
